title: Periodic UV-reflective SWIR-transmissive dichroic stack using HfO2/SiO2
scientific_hypothesis: A periodic alternating stack of HfO2 and SiO2 layers, with individual thicknesses tuned around quarter-wave optical thickness at 300 nm center UV wavelength, will produce high reflectance in 200-400 nm while maintaining high transmittance in 800-1500 nm, with performance improving as pair count increases up to the 30-layer limit.
design_principle: Distributed Bragg reflector physics: alternating high and low refractive index layers create constructive interference for reflection at wavelengths where optical thickness equals λ/4. At longer wavelengths (SWIR band), the same physical thicknesses represent much less than quarter-wave optical thickness, reducing interference effects and allowing high transmission. The index contrast between HfO2 and SiO2 determines reflection bandwidth and peak reflectance.
proposed_topology: air / hfo2 / sio2 / hfo2 / sio2 / hfo2 / sio2 / hfo2 / sio2 / hfo2 / sio2 / hfo2 / sio2 / hfo2 / sio2 / hfo2 / sio2 / hfo2 / sio2 / hfo2 / sio2 / fused_silica
soft_objectives: Maximize mean transmittance in 800-1500 nm band
Maximize mean reflectance in 200-400 nm band
Keep total layer count at exactly 20 layers (10 pairs)
manufacturing_considerations: Total layer count fixed at 20 to stay well under 30-layer limit
Individual layer thicknesses should remain in manufacturable range (approximately 20-100 nm for UV quarter-wave design)
HfO2 and SiO2 are both standard evaporated/sputtered coating materials
theory_basis: Quarter-wave stack reflectance increases with number of layer pairs and with refractive index contrast between high and low index materials
HfO2 has higher refractive index than SiO2 in visible and near-UV wavelengths, making it suitable as the high-index layer in a Bragg reflector
Optical thickness equal to λ/4 at target wavelength produces maximum constructive interference for reflection at that wavelength
At wavelengths significantly longer than the quarter-wave design wavelength, the same physical thickness produces less interference, allowing higher transmission
Fused silica substrate is transparent in both UV and SWIR bands, so substrate absorption is not a limiting factor in these bands
expected_advantages: Simple periodic topology is well-understood and easy to optimize
20 layers provides substantial design freedom while leaving margin under the 30-layer constraint
HfO2/SiO2 material pair is industry-standard for UV-visible-NIR coatings with good environmental durability
Quarter-wave center at 300 nm places the reflection band center within the 200-400 nm UV suppression target
known_risks: Refractive index values for hfo2 and sio2 at UV wavelengths are recalled approximately; actual dispersion data from the material catalog may differ and affect optimal thickness values
The exact quarter-wave thickness calculation depends on n(λ) at 300 nm which I estimate as n_HfO2 ≈ 1.95 and n_SiO2 ≈ 1.46, but these need verification from catalog data
20 layers may not achieve sufficient UV reflectance if index contrast is lower than recalled; may need to increase pair count toward 30 layers
Incidence angle is not specified in the request; I assume normal incidence (0 degrees) but oblique angles would shift the reflection band
Polarization is not specified; at non-normal incidence, s and p polarizations will split in performance
No anti-reflection treatment on the air-side entrance surface is included; this could reduce SWIR transmission slightly
Long-term UV durability of HfO2/SiO2 stack under high-altitude conditions is not addressed in this optical design
execution_request_english: Design a planar multilayer dielectric film with air incidence on a fused_silica substrate. Use exactly 20 layers in alternating sequence: hfo2, SiO2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos), hfo2, SiO2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos), hfo2, SiO2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos), hfo2, SiO2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos), hfo2, SiO2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos), hfo2, SiO2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos), hfo2, SiO2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos), hfo2, SiO2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos), hfo2, SiO2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos), hfo2, SiO2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos). Optimize individual layer thicknesses in nanometers to maximize transmittance in 800-1500 nm wavelength band and maximize reflectance in 200-400 nm wavelength band. Assume normal incidence (0 degrees) and unpolarized light. Total layer count is fixed at 20. Materials are restricted to hfo2 and SiO2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos) only. Report best_target_score, valid_candidates, tightest_margin, run_status, and thicknesses_nm for each optimization round.
